event_text: First War of Scottish Independence: James Douglas leads a raid into Weardale and almost kills Edward III of England.
headline: English King Narrowly Escapes Death in Weardale Raid
story: Barry perched on a stone wall, gazing out at the chaos below. 'Seems James Douglas has brought his brand of Scottish enthusiasm to Weardale, Susan. 1327, and the First War of Scottish Independence is in full swing. He's leading a wee raid, trying to catch the English off guard.' Susan cocked her head. 'And nearly managed to kill the young Edward III, by all accounts. Just a lad, really – not even king yet, still a prince. His father, Edward II, is still on the throne, but not for much longer, if gossip's to be believed.' Barry snorted. 'Douglas and his men descended upon the English camp, hoping to take out the future king. Brave, if a bit foolhardy. I mean, killing the heir to the throne might've simplified things, strategically speaking, but it's not exactly the most subtle approach.' Susan rustled her feathers. 'Still, it's a bold statement – the Scots won't be pushed around, and they'll take the fight to English soil if need be.'
regret_line: A missed opportunity to shorten the impending centuries of Anglo-Scottish bickering by a few decades.
winner_line: The concept of perpetual border skirmishes and entrenched national distrust.
